title: Data Brokers & Data Collection Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to protect yourself from data brokers. Learn how to opt out, limit data collection, and secure your personal information.
intro: Data brokers collect and sell your personal information without your direct consent. This comprehensive checklist helps you identify what data is being collected, opt out of major data broker services, and implement protective measures to limit future data harvesting.

items.why: Understanding what information is publicly available helps you prioritize protection efforts and identify potential privacy risks.
items.howTo: Search for yourself on Google, social media, and people search sites. Document what information appears including addresses, phone numbers, family members, and employment history.

items.task: Check major data broker sites for your information
items.why: Data brokers like Whitepages, Spokeo, and BeenVerified often have detailed profiles that can be used for identity theft or harassment.
items.howTo: Search for yourself on major data broker sites: Whitepages, Spokeo, BeenVerified, PeopleFinder, Intelius, and TruePeopleSearch. Take screenshots of any profiles found.

items.task: Map your digital footprint across platforms
items.why: Social media and online accounts are primary sources for data brokers to collect and correlate your personal information.
items.howTo: List all your social media accounts, online shopping accounts, and service subscriptions. Review privacy settings and public information on each platform.

items.task: Opt out of major data broker services
items.why: Removing your information from major data brokers significantly reduces your exposure and makes it harder for others to find your personal details.
items.howTo: Visit opt-out pages for Whitepages, Spokeo, BeenVerified, PeopleFinder, Intelius, TruePeopleSearch, and Instant Checkmate. Follow their removal processes, which may require ID verification.

items.task: Remove yourself from marketing and mailing lists
items.why: Marketing databases are often sold to data brokers and contribute to the proliferation of your personal information across multiple platforms.
items.howTo: Register with DMAchoice.org for direct mail opt-out, use OptOutPrescreen.com for credit offers, and unsubscribe from unwanted email lists systematically.

items.task: Set up ongoing monitoring for new data broker listings
items.why: Data brokers continuously add new information, so one-time removal isn't sufficient for long-term privacy protection.
items.howTo: Create Google Alerts for your name and contact information. Schedule quarterly checks of major data broker sites. Consider using a paid removal service for ongoing monitoring.

items.why: Web browsers collect extensive data about your online activities, which is often sold to data brokers and advertisers.
items.howTo: Switch to Incognito Browser for enhanced privacy protection. Enable tracking protection, disable third-party cookies, and use privacy-focused search engines like DuckDuckGo.

items.why: Social media platforms are major sources of personal information that data brokers use to build comprehensive profiles.
items.howTo: Set all social media profiles to private, limit friend/follower lists visibility, disable location tracking, and remove personal information from bio sections.

items.task: Protect your phone number from data collection
items.why: Phone numbers are key identifiers that data brokers use to link various pieces of information together to create detailed profiles.
items.howTo: Use Google Voice or similar services for online accounts, enable caller ID blocking, and avoid giving your real number to retailers or surveys.

items.task: Create separate emails for different purposes
items.why: Using the same email across multiple services makes it easier for data brokers to correlate your activities and build comprehensive profiles.
items.howTo: Create separate email addresses for shopping, social media, financial accounts, and subscriptions. Use email aliases when possible to further compartmentalize your identity.

items.why: Privacy laws like CCPA and GDPR give you legal rights to know what data is collected and request deletion from companies.
items.howTo: Submit data deletion requests to companies under CCPA (California residents) or GDPR (EU residents). Keep records of all requests and follow up on non-compliance.

items.task: Set up credit monitoring and freeze your credit
items.why: Data broker information is often used for identity theft, making credit monitoring essential for early detection of fraudulent activity.
items.howTo: Place credit freezes with all three major credit bureaus (Experian, Equifax, TransUnion). Set up free credit monitoring through your bank or credit card company.
